snapshot.topic: ecological community control, microbiome, and chemostat reaction systems

claims.statement: For locally Lipschitz dissipative ecological equations x_i'=x_i f_i(z), y'=g(z), assume (A3a) every missing-species invasion rate is nonzero for every boundary ergodic measure, (A3b) signs for a missing species are constant across ergodic measures with the same species support, and the invasion graph is acyclic. If each -i community has positive invasion rate for its absent species i, Hofbauer-Schreiber Corollary 1 implies robust permanence. A twice continuously differentiable system with a boundary subcommunity at which every missing species has a negative invasion rate is not permanent (their Remark 3).
assumptions: A1: locally Lipschitz species and auxiliary dynamics
A2: a compact global attractor / dissipativity
A3a and A3b sign conditions over all relevant boundary ergodic measures
acyclic invasion graph
negative-rate nonpermanence conclusion additionally assumes twice continuous differentiability
claims.status: established_external_theorem; theorem statement and assumptions reconstructed from primary source, proof not independently reproduced
claims.proof_path: FINAL_REPORT.md; hofbauer_schreiber_invasion.txt lines 52-80 (model and A1-A2), 81-110 (ergodic invasion rates and A3), 122-136 (Theorem 1, negative-rate falsifier, -i corollary)
claims.novelty_boundary: Classical published theorem; this work does not claim novelty. The theorem requires all relevant ergodic boundary measures and acyclicity, not only the observed stable resident cycles.
claims.costs: For a periodic chemostat, must acquire resident boundary cycles or measures, phase-resolved rates/resources, and missing-species growth-response data. Complete boundary-measure enumeration and cycle certification are not provided by a generic algorithm here.
claims.falsifier: Under the smoothness assumptions, find a terminal boundary community with every missing strain's measured or certified long-run invasion rate strictly negative. For a claimed positive control window, a reliably negative invasion rate on a required -i community falsifies that model-level prediction.
claims.next_gate: Acquire all boundary ergodic supports and use validated Poincare-map or interval methods to certify invasion signs and graph acyclicity for the selected model.

claims.statement: In the cyclic May-Leonard competitive Lotka-Volterra system x1'=x1(1-x1-beta x2-alpha x3), x2'=x2(1-alpha x1-x2-beta x3), x3'=x3(1-beta x1-alpha x2-x3), take alpha=0.8 and beta=1.3. At each single-species equilibrium one absent strain invades at rate 1-alpha=+0.2 while the other has rate 1-beta=-0.3, yet the boundary supports an attracting heteroclinic cycle and the system is not permanent. Thus singleton invasion information without invasion-graph acyclicity is insufficient.
assumptions: Cyclic May-Leonard competition equations as written
alpha=0.8<1 and alpha+beta=2.1>2, a stable heteroclinic-cycle regime
claims.status: established_primary_model_result; equation and signs reconstructed; classic theorem not independently proved here
claims.proof_path: FINAL_REPORT.md acyclicity counterexample paragraph; Hofbauer-Schreiber 2022 discussion; May-Leonard 1975 primary source
claims.novelty_boundary: Classical counterexample, not a new result. It shows why invasion-graph acyclicity cannot be omitted.
claims.costs: Three-species ODE and exact linear invasion-rate evaluations at the axis equilibria; no simulation or empirical data needed to obtain these signs.
claims.falsifier: A derivation showing the stated parameters do not yield the attracting heteroclinic boundary cycle, or an interior uniform lower bound for all three densities, would refute the nonpermanence claim.
claims.next_gate: Use as a negative control when translating boundary invasion measurements into intervention guarantees; compute cycles and multi-species boundary communities as well as singleton rates.

claims.statement: For the published three-strain periodically diluted Monod chemostat with D0=0.4675, omega=0.2, R0=11, alpha=(1,0.7,0.64), beta=(1,0.3,0.2), fixed-step RK4 estimates r3|{1,2}=+2.4657387e-5 and r2|{1,3}=+3.6260939e-5 per time unit at a=0.300; r3|{1,2}=-1.9908408e-4 at a=0.325; r2|{1,3}=-1.2608377e-4 at a=0.275; and both missing-strain rates at {3} are negative at a=0.200. Numerical bisection estimates the first two zeros at a≈0.3031558 and a≈0.29493995. At a=0.300 a species-2-only resident orbit is also found, with r1=+0.02158096 and r3=-0.00347006, which qualifies numerically as an additional candidate -1 community under the source definition.
assumptions: Uses beta2=+0.3 from the paper figure caption; paper body prints beta2=-0.3, unresolved source conflict
Fixed-step RK4 integrates periodic resident orbits and accumulated log invasion coordinates
A candidate coexistence window requires all other signs, A3 sign consistency, and acyclicity; these are not fully certified
claims.status: finite_numerical_diagnostic; not interval-certified; full model-level permanence classification UNKNOWN
claims.proof_path: reproduce_chemostat.py; refine_invasion_rates.py; invasion_rates_rk4.json; FINAL_REPORT.md numerical table; source parameter conflict at hofbauer_schreiber_invasion.txt lines 183 and 201-202
claims.novelty_boundary: Reproduction and threshold refinement of a published numerical example, not a theorem or experimentally established coexistence window. The extra species-2-only -1 node conflicts with the paper's claim that only {1,2} and {1,3} are -i communities, but it is itself invadable and does not reverse the permanence prediction.
claims.costs: Period T=31.4159265; 240-1920 RK4 steps per period for reported key orbits, periodic-map iteration, two scalar bisections, and 2,001 initial resources for the species-2 resident Poincare map. No validated numerics or experimental data.
claims.falsifier: Independent high-accuracy or validated integration changes a reported sign, the species-2 resident orbit is not physical/stable on the x1=0 face, or the intended beta2 parameter is negative rather than positive. An experiment producing opposite rare-invader log slopes under the same fitted model also falsifies its prediction.
claims.next_gate: Resolve beta2 against Wolkowicz-Zhao 1998; certify every relevant boundary orbit/ergodic sign using interval enclosures; establish A3 and graph acyclicity; then test rare invasion experimentally under matched-mean constant and periodic dilution.

claims.statement: The pinned Astra P/N33 manuscript states a common compact convex classwise absorber for every finite endotactic exponent-arrow diagram with rate paths k_e(t) measurable in [kappa,K], 0<kappa<=K<infinity. Every initial state in a positive stoichiometric class has a unique global positive solution and enters the same absorber in a finite time bound independent of the rate path.
assumptions: Finite actual exponent-arrow diagram is endotactic under the essential-source definition
Positive class P=(c+S) intersect R^d_{>0} is supplied
Every edge coefficient remains in a supplied common interval [kappa,K] with positive lower endpoint
Deterministic Caratheodory ODE; not a stochastic jump process, delay system, or arbitrary exogenous forcing model
claims.status: source_derived_unreviewed_candidate; external correctness and priority unresolved
claims.proof_path: astra/N33-endotactic-permanence.txt; pinned evidence page d-326696af15b5e02b.html; local reconstruction endotactic_permanence.tex lines 51-118 (contract/theorem), 396-517 (weighted essential-source drift), 618-737 (finite entry/absorption), 742-807 (common-span switching), 809-856 (span counterexample), 1030-1109 (scope and resource limits)
claims.novelty_boundary: Astra's card attributes the affine construction to OpenAI family 149 and labels the theorem source-derived/unreviewed. It does not apply directly to the Monod chemostat unless its actual kinetic exponent-arrow diagram satisfies the stated endotactic rate-box contract. It supplies existence, not an efficient compiler or useful general entry bound.
claims.costs: Finite network, stoichiometric class, rate interval, affine family and offsets are supplied/precomputed. The source states no useful bound on family size, precision, activity cutoff, absorber scale, or waiting time.
claims.falsifier: A finite endotactic diagram and admissible bounded positive measurable coefficient path with a positive-class solution that becomes extinct or unbounded would refute the candidate theorem. Removing the lower rate bound already admits the exact 0<->A extinction example in proof lines 1030-1043.
claims.next_gate: Independent expert proof audit focused on the affine activity lemma, all-ties essential-source drift, and scale-iteration absorption; separately determine if an experimental reaction system's actual kinetic law is in the theorem's input class.

claims.statement: Given a supplied positive inward polytope certificate with strict facet collars, a bounded molecular jump-rate control family, and lattice-compatible initial counts with a positive concentration-scale buffer, Astra P/N35 provides an explicit upper bound Pr(tau_Q<=T)<=sum_i exp(-theta_i V g_i(X0))+2m V Lambda T exp(-c_* V) for every finite T and predictable control. Taking T=exp(c_*V/2) yields an exponentially long finite horizon.
assumptions: Integer nonnegative complexes with exact falling-factorial propensities
Supplied compact positive polytope and strict inward drift collar for every allowed mode
Bounded predictable controls and rate envelope
Lattice-compatible initial point with fixed positive facet gaps
This is finite-horizon safety, not all-time survival, nonexplosion outside the stopped region, or stochastic permanence
claims.status: source_derived_unreviewed_candidate with reported internal proof; exact theorem reconstructed locally, no external validation
claims.proof_path: astra/N35-controlled-chemical-safety.txt; pinned evidence d-bea4150c129f63b3.html; local jump_safety.txt lines 5-31 (contract), 33-69 (factorial correction/parameters), 71-123 (stopped Dynkin proof and horizon), plus endotactic_permanence.tex lines 1236-1275
claims.novelty_boundary: Does not transfer N33 deterministic absorption to infinite-time stochastic survival. A positive deterministic interior is not enough; the strict inward polytope and finite-volume collar are separate supplied premises.
claims.costs: Must acquire certificate polytope, rational facet margins/layers, rate/volume bounds, initial integer counts and reaction-lattice feasibility. Safety horizon and error depend exponentially on volume; source example notes direct thinning could be computationally prohibitive.
claims.falsifier: For a certified model and supplied controls, an observed/theoretically possible exit probability exceeding the bound at a finite T would refute the candidate certificate theorem; first audit propensities, facet margins, overshoot, and control class.
claims.next_gate: Independently replay an exact example and test whether measured intervention modes share a common strict collar; never infer infinite-time stationary tightness from this finite-time result.

claims.statement: The pinned Astra U/N77 summary reports a deficiency-zero complex-balanced network with one deterministic classwise global attractor but an infinite sequence of closed irreducible positive recurrent stochastic classes in the same linear stoichiometric plane whose stationary distributions escape every common compact set. It refutes only the transfer to uniform tightness across components, not componentwise positive recurrence.
assumptions: Use of the reported specific network and class family
Claim is summary-only; detailed proof/code absent from supplied evidence
claims.status: source_reported_only; not independently reconstructed; historical priority unresolved
claims.proof_path: astra/N77-stationary-tightness-counterexample.txt lines 1-12; linked summary-only source page d-14513a2bef6ac3df.html
claims.novelty_boundary: Does not show an individual class is transient or null recurrent. No external novelty claim.
claims.costs: To promote beyond source-reported, acquire and verify the full stochastic class invariant, stationary balance equations, and deterministic global-attractor proof assumptions.
claims.falsifier: A counterexample to the stated closed-class decomposition, irreducibility/positive recurrence, or escaping stationary-mass calculation would invalidate this specific boundary claim.
claims.next_gate: Retrieve the full N77 proof/code if a stochastic permanence synthesis depends on it, and separately state recurrence componentwise versus uniformly across a stoichiometric class.
